nodes.title: Decode + Blend (stage 1)
widgets_values:
## Decode + Blend (stage 1)

Decodes the stage-1 latent with the native tiled VAE decode and
**Laplacian-pyramid blends** it with the inpaint reference. The blend **dilation**
is crucial - increase it if low frequencies bleed into the blend area.

Tiling is exposed on the node: `512 / 64 / 128 / 32` suits most hardware. Fewer,
larger tiles run faster but need more memory.

nodes.title: Preprocess - Stage 2
widgets_values:
## Preprocess - Stage 2

VAE-encodes the blended stage-1 result, re-conditions on the high-res start image, and re-attaches the frozen audio for the high-resolution refinement pass.

nodes.title: Decode + Blend (stage 2)
widgets_values:
## Decode + Blend (stage 2)

Decodes the high-res latent (video and audio) with the native tiled VAE decode and
does the **final Laplacian-pyramid blend** with the original video for a seamless
transition, then assembles the output video.

Tiling is exposed on the node: `512 / 64 / 128 / 32` suits most hardware. Fewer,
larger tiles run faster but need more memory.

nodes.title: How to use — Outpainting
widgets_values:
# How to Use Outpainting

This workflow supports **outpainting** (extending the canvas beyond the original frame). You provide a mask telling the model where to generate, and an optional prompt describing what should be there.

## 1. No prompt = the simple case

- without a prompt → just extends the existing canvas. The model fills the new area to match the surrounding scene.


## 2. Prompts describe the scene, not the edit

It's not an edit tool. Write a regular T2V-style prompt describing the out-painting region.



## 3. Green leftovers

The pipeline composites green under the mask before diffusion — sometimes traces leak through at mask edges. Try a bigger dilation, a different seed, or re-encode the mask losslessly or the blending parameter is very important.

Make sure to click the "Agree and Access" button the first time you download.

- [ IC-LoRA In/Outpainting - ltx-2.3-22b-ic-lora-in-outpainting-0.9.safetensors ](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-In-Outpainting/blob/main/ltx-2.3-22b-ic-lora-in-outpainting-0.9.safetensors)

**Text Encoder - finetuned for LTX-2.5**
- [gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/blob/main/text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-bf16.safetensors)

│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │      └── ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors
│   │      └── ltx-2.5-video-vae-conv-bf16.safetensors / ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors

nodes.title: Input Parameters
widgets_values:
## Input Parameters

Encodes the prompt and prepares the two input videos: extracts frames, fps and
audio, builds the mask (`ImageToMask`), resizes to each stage's resolution and
**dilates** the mask - set **mask dilation radius** to suit the object.

**Prompt enhancement** is optional. Turn on **Enhance positive prompt** to rewrite
the prompt into a fuller description; the workflow picks the image-aware enhancer
when **use image input** is on and the text-only one otherwise. **enhancer_seed**
makes that rewrite reproducible. The negative prompt is used as written.

**use image input** also derives `bypass_i2v`, so the optional start image is only
conditioned on when you actually supply one.

**Save memory (LTX API):** paste a key into **LTX API key** and the prompt is
encoded and enhanced through the API instead of the local Gemma models. The
workflow switches over on its own whenever a key is present - there is nothing to
un-bypass.

Note: the output **dimensions and length** are derived later in **Preprocess**,
from the masked frames, not here.

nodes.title: Preprocess
widgets_values:
## Preprocess (stage 1)

Masks the frames (`LTXVInpaintPreprocess`), builds the empty AV latent **at the reference video's size/length** (GetImageSize is here), conditions on the optional start image, injects the IC-LoRA guide, and adds **frozen audio** (VAEEncodeAudio → SetAudioRefTokens).

*Frozen audio keeps the result consistent with the original sound; remove the audio stream if you don't want that guidance.*
